description: One rule: shipping to HERE needs THAT document. This is the compliance-rules-driven half of the module and the reason a new export market is a row rather than a release — a farm that lands a buyer in Vietnam adds the documents Vietnam asks for and the next shipment to Vietnam builds its own checklist. The lookup is by tier first and country second: a Local or Domestic rule leaves the country empty and applies to every shipment at that tier, and an International rule names the country it is about. A COUNTRY RULE ADDS TO THE TIER'S RULES RATHER THAN REPLACING THEM, because the paper a country asks for is on top of the paper an export always needs, never instead of it.

fields.description: Which tier this rule is about. Local and Domestic rules leave the country empty and apply to every shipment at that tier; International rules name a country.
fields.label: Destination Tier

fields.description: The country this rule is about, for an International rule. EMPTY MEANS EVERY COUNTRY AT THIS TIER — which is how the documents every export needs (an AES declaration, a certificate of origin) are stated once rather than copied per country. A country's own rules are read IN ADDITION to those, never instead of them.
fields.label: Destination Country

fields.description: The document this destination asks for.
fields.label: Trade Document Template

fields.description: Whether the shipment is held for this document or merely offered it. A REQUIRED document blocks 'Ready to Ship' where enforcement is on and is named in every readiness answer; an unrequired one is created as a placeholder and tracked, which is the right shape for paper a buyer usually wants and no rule compels.
fields.label: Required

fields.description: A disabled rule is not applied to new shipments. It is how a requirement that a destination has dropped is withdrawn without deleting the record of what used to be asked for — which an audit of a shipment made last season will want.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Scope this rule to one Company. EMPTY MEANS EVERY COMPANY on the site, which is the ordinary case — the paper Japan asks for does not depend on which of an operator's entities is shipping. Set it only where two entities on one site genuinely ship under different arrangements.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: Where this document sits in the checklist, overriding the template's own sequence for this destination. Lower first.
fields.label: Sequence

fields.description: Why this destination asks for this, and anything the sales desk needs to know about getting it — who issues it, how long it takes, what holds it up. On an ePhyto this is where 'lodged in PCIT, allow three working days, inspection must be booked first' belongs.
fields.label: Notes

fields.description: Set on the requirements this app seeds. A SHIPPED REQUIREMENT IS NOT OVERWRITTEN once an operator has edited it, and the seeder writes a rule only where no rule for that destination and template exists at all — because the seeded set is this app's reading of a general case, and the operator's is their own broker's reading of their own trade.
fields.label: Shipped Default

name: Destination Document Requirement
